description: Practical introduction to computational genomics and bioinformatics. Lectures include sequencing and genomic techniques. Labs include command-line programming, data processing and visualizing in R, genome assembly, RNA-seq analysis, sequence alignment, variant calling and basic population genomics. Engagement with primary genomics literature. Analysis of genomic data as a final project.
preAndCorequisites:
• Complete all of:
    • BIOL230 - Principles of Genetics (1.5)
    • BIOL361 - Molecular Genetics and Genomics (1.5)
supplementalNotes:
• Credit will be granted for only one of BIOL 469, BIOL 470 (if taken in the same topic), BIOL 550E (if taken in the same topic), BIOL 569.
  • A combined undergraduate and graduate course.
title: Introduction to Computational Genomics
